title: Toward a better trade-off between performance and fairness with kernel-based distribution matching
findings: This paper does not contain any findings related to religion, as it is not a subject of the research. The key findings relate to a proposed 'MinDiff' framework using Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) which achieves a better trade-off between model accuracy and fairness (specifically, reducing the False Positive Rate gap between subgroups) compared to correlation-based methods.

measurement_description: The paper does not measure any benchmarks related to faith or religion. The study focuses on fairness metrics, specifically the False Positive Rate Gap (FPRgap), in the context of income prediction, using 'sex' as the sensitive attribute.
